title: feat: let a caller supply its own user-facing error strings
description:
Found while migrating `variant-reviewer` onto biohttp 0.1.0.

`http_error_message()` returns fixed English strings with no hook to override them. Once an app adopts biohttp, `res$error` is what its UI shows, so the wording changes without anyone editing UI code.

Four of six messages differed from the app's own:

| case | app | biohttp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 404 | No X data was found for this query. | *(same)* |
| 429 | X is busy right now (too many requests). Please try again in a moment. | X is busy right now. Please try again in a moment. |
| 5xx | X is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly. | X is temporarily unavailable. Please try again. |
| other | Couldn't retrieve data from X right now. | Could not retrieve data from X right now. |
| timeout | X took too long to respond. Please try again shortly. | X took too long to respond. Please try again. |
| DNS | Couldn't reach X. Please check your internet connection and try again. | Could not reach X. Check your connection. |

The app's test asserting the DNS message mentions checking your internet connection fails after the move. Nothing technical leaks in either version, so this is wording rather than a safety problem.

## Not a bug

The biohttp strings are good, and splitting `error` (for a person) from `detail` (for a log) is the right design. The gap is that there is no way to keep an app's own voice, or to localise, while adopting the transport.

## Options

1. An option, e.g. `biohttp.error_message`, taking a function `(source, http, condition)` that biohttp calls instead of its built-in.
2. Leave the code alone and document that an app with its own voice should build the message itself from `res$status` and `res$http` and ignore `res$error`.

Option 2 may well be enough, but it is currently undocumented, and the failure mode is a UI string changing without any UI change in the diff.

title: feat: bound the cache by entry count as well as age and size
description:
Found while migrating `variant-reviewer` onto biohttp 0.1.0.

`build_cache()` configures `cachem::cache_mem()` with `max_age` and `max_size` only. `cachem` also supports `max_n`, and biohttp does not pass it, so there is no ceiling on the number of entries.

```r
deparse(body(biohttp:::build_cache))
#> cachem::cache_mem(max_age = env_num("BIOHTTP_CACHE_TTL", 1800),
#>                   max_size = env_num("BIOHTTP_CACHE_MAX_SIZE", 256 * 1024^2))

names(formals(cachem::cache_mem))
#> "max_size" "max_age" "max_n" "evict" "missing" "logfile"
```

## Why it matters

The app being migrated had:

```r
cachem::cache_mem(
  max_age  = VR_CACHE_TTL,
  max_size = VR_CACHE_MAX_SIZE,
  max_n    = 5000,          # <- no biohttp equivalent
  evict    = "lru"
)
```

Moving to biohttp drops that bound silently. A total-size ceiling bounds bytes, not entries, so a long-running server answering many small responses can hold far more entries than the app previously permitted. Its test asserting the cache is bounded by entry count now fails, and the honest value to report is `Inf`.

## Proposal

Read `BIOHTTP_CACHE_MAX_N` alongside the existing two and pass it to `cache_mem(max_n = )`, defaulting to `cachem`'s own default so present behaviour is unchanged unless set.

Worth considering at the same time: `evict = "lru"` is `cachem`'s default, but setting it explicitly would make the eviction policy part of the documented contract rather than an inherited default.

title: fix: cache_reset() silently invalidates a held cache reference
description:
Found while migrating `variant-reviewer` onto biohttp 0.1.0.

`cache_reset()` sets `cache_store$store <- NULL`, so the next `cache()` call builds a **new** object. Any reference taken before the reset keeps pointing at the orphaned store. Writes through it go nowhere the rest of the package can see, and reads return stale entries. Nothing errors or warns.

## Reproduce (biohttp 0.1.0)

```r
held <- biohttp::cache()
held$set("k", list(ok = TRUE, v = 1))

biohttp::cache_reset()

live <- biohttp::cache()
held$size()            # 1
live$size()            # 0
identical(held, live)  # FALSE

held$set("k2", list(ok = TRUE, v = 2))
live$exists("k2")      # FALSE
```

## Why it bit

The app kept its cache as a plain object (`vr_cache`) and exposed `vr_cache$size()` and `vr_cache$reset()`. The obvious migration is `vr_cache <- biohttp::cache()`, and it is wrong: after any reset the app reads a cache nothing writes to, and the only symptom is a hit rate that quietly goes to zero.

The workaround was an active binding, which is not something a caller should have to work out:

```r
makeActiveBinding("vr_cache", function() biohttp::cache(), environment())
```

## Options

1. `cache_reset()` calls `$reset()` on the existing store instead of dropping it, so held references stay valid.
2. Keep the current behaviour and document it, including that `cache()` must be called fresh each time rather than stored.

Option 1 gives up rebuilding the store from changed environment variables on reset, which may be deliberate. Raising rather than sending a patch for that reason.
